summary: Polygon's Toussaint Egan and other staff curate one top recent pick for each major streaming service, with 'also good' alternatives. The October 2023 update added Castlevania: Nocturne, Gen V, Hijack, and The Continental. Picks span Netflix, Hulu, Prime Video, Max, Disney Plus, Paramount Plus, Apple TV Plus, and Peacock.
one_line: Polygon's updated guide picks the best new TV series on each major streaming platform, with runner-up recommendations per service.
key_facts: The latest update to Polygon's list added Castlevania: Nocturne, Gen V, Hijack, and The Continental.
Netflix pick: Castlevania: Nocturne, created by Clive Bradley, follows Richter Belmont three centuries after the original series, set amid the French Revolution.
The original Castlevania was a 32-episode adult animated series produced by Powerhouse Animation Studios that premiered in 2017.
Hulu pick: Reservation Dogs, created by Sterlin Harjo and produced by Taika Waititi, about misfits on a reservation in Oklahoma; its third season ended the show.
Prime Video pick: Gen V, from showrunners Michele Fazekas and Tara Butters, is set at Godolkin University in the universe of The Boys and stars Jaz Sinclair as Marie.
Max pick: Unicorn: Warriors Eternal, created by Genndy Tartakovsky and Darrick Bachman, is a fantasy action series over two decades in the making.
Disney Plus pick: Andor, created by Tony Gilroy, held the No. 1 spot on Polygon's list of the best shows of 2022; Diego Luna stars as Cassian Andor and Stellan Skarsgård plays Luthen Rael.
Paramount Plus pick: The Good Fight, created by Robert and Michelle King, began in 2017 with Diane Lockhart (Christine Baranski) and is described as 'the Star Trek of legal dramas'.
Apple TV Plus pick: Hijack, created by George Kay and Jim Field Smith, stars Idris Elba as Sam Nelson on a hijacked plane and is told in close to real time.
Peacock pick: The Continental: From the World of John Wick, with fights led by Larnell Stovall, runs three episodes.
Gen V's 'also good' list notes that A League of Their Own and Paper Girls were each canceled after one season.
Peacock's alternatives include Poker Face, Rian Johnson's series starring Natasha Lyonne, and Girls5Eva.
